title: Narrating the Names of (Mughal) Custodians (All these petitioners had approached

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Emperor (Bahadur Shah) put (the Pathan Commanders) from kasur, At the head of the Mughal forces (marching towards Punjab). These army commanders included Shams Khan1 and Jalaludin, As well as Bajida khan2 followed by their troops. (1)
lines: The Emperor (Bahadur Shah) put (the Pathan Commanders) from kasur,
At the head of the Mughal forces (marching towards Punjab).
These army commanders included Shams Khan1 and Jalaludin,
As well as Bajida khan2 followed by their troops.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
These army commanders had been the custodians of Traori, Whom the Singhs had ransacked and tortured them as well.
Mahawat Khan3 and Farzul Khan4 (among the warriors), Claimed themselves to be highly muscular and brave. (2)
lines: Mahawat Khan3 and Farzul Khan4 (among the warriors),
Claimed themselves to be highly muscular and brave.

blocks.text: They, too, had accompanied Wazir Khan (during the battle of Sirhind) Whom (Banda Bahadur and Singhs) had ransacked and tortured. The (erstwhile) custodians of Kunjpura5 and Samana6 too were included, As well as the custodians of Sadhaura7 and the areas across the Yamuna8 . (3)
lines: They, too, had accompanied Wazir Khan (during the battle of Sirhind) Whom (Banda Bahadur and Singhs) had ransacked and tortured.
The (erstwhile) custodians of Kunjpura5 and Samana6 too were included,
As well as the custodians of Sadhaura7 and the areas across the Yamuna8 .

blocks.text: All these (eastwhile) custodians had fought along Wazir Khan, Whom Banda Singh had humbled and defeated. All these who had come together as petitioners (to the Emperor), Were despatched to lead the Mughal forces after a deep thought. (4)
lines: All these (eastwhile) custodians had fought along Wazir Khan,
Whom Banda Singh had humbled and defeated.
All these who had come together as petitioners (to the Emperor),
Were despatched to lead the Mughal forces after a deep thought.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The (Emperor) had sent them to lead the Mughal troops, In order to ascertain (the might and intentions of Banda Singh). After hearing the news of Banda Singh's grant of passage to him, The emperor had felt delighted (at the turn of events). (5)
lines: The (Emperor) had sent them to lead the Mughal troops,
In order to ascertain (the might and intentions of Banda Singh).
After hearing the news of Banda Singh's grant of passage to him,
The emperor had felt delighted (at the turn of events).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Bahadur Shah felt reassured (after the grant of passage), And felt relieved and delighted after reaching Lahore. He returned to Delhi after spending a few days at Lahore, But he could not reach Delhi (as he died on the way). (6)
lines: Bahadur Shah felt reassured (after the grant of passage),
And felt relieved and delighted after reaching Lahore.
He returned to Delhi after spending a few days at Lahore,
But he could not reach Delhi (as he died on the way).

blocks.text: He was survived by his four young sons, Who perished as a result of internecine war among themselves. Many years passed in this state of chaos and uncertainty, That is what Rattan Singh (the author) had heard about this period. (7)
lines: He was survived by his four young sons,
Who perished as a result of internecine war among themselves.
Many years passed in this state of chaos and uncertainty,
That is what Rattan Singh (the author) had heard about this period.

blocks.text: The Reign of Farrukhsiar*
Dohra:

(The Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah died (during his return from Lahore), In the year one thousand seven hundred and eighty four10 . Now (dear readers) listen to the further account of, Farukhsiar, who was the grandson of Bahadur Shah. (1)
lines: (The Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah died (during his return from Lahore),
In the year one thousand seven hundred and eighty four10 .
Now (dear readers) listen to the further account of,
Farukhsiar, who was the grandson of Bahadur Shah.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

When Farukhsiar succeeded to the Mughal throne, Some slanderers (of Sikhs) incited the king (against Banda Singh). They reported that Guru's disciple Banda Singh had created havoc, While they lived in peace in rest of the Mughal empire. (2)
lines: When Farukhsiar succeeded to the Mughal throne,
Some slanderers (of Sikhs) incited the king (against Banda Singh).
They reported that Guru's disciple Banda Singh had created havoc,
While they lived in peace in rest of the Mughal empire.

blocks.text: Revenue collections were pouring (into the treasury) from twenty two provinces, And everyone (except the Sikhs) obeyed the royal edicts. They incited the new emperor to chastise and subdue Banda Singh, So that his grand father's mission could be accomplished. (3)
lines: Revenue collections were pouring (into the treasury) from twenty two provinces,
And everyone (except the Sikhs) obeyed the royal edicts.
They incited the new emperor to chastise and subdue Banda Singh,
So that his grand father's mission could be accomplished.

blocks.text: Dohra:

(Thereupon) Farukhsiar responded to (their instigations) by saying, That his grand father (Bahadur Shah) had given him an advice. He had advised that there existed a house (dynasty) of Nanak, With whom he (Farukhsiar) must not enter into any conflict. (4)
lines: (Thereupon) Farukhsiar responded to (their instigations) by saying,
That his grand father (Bahadur Shah) had given him an advice.
He had advised that there existed a house (dynasty) of Nanak,
With whom he (Farukhsiar) must not enter into any conflict.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

When his great grand father (Aurangzeb) had felt offended (witht he Guru), He had ordered Farukhsiar's grandfather to wage a war against the Guru. But his grandfather (Bahadurshah) did not proceed against the Guru, And sent his soldiers to work in favour of the Guru. (5)
lines: When his great grand father (Aurangzeb) had felt offended (witht he Guru),
He had ordered Farukhsiar's grandfather to wage a war against the Guru.
But his grandfather (Bahadurshah) did not proceed against the Guru,
And sent his soldiers to work in favour of the Guru.

blocks.text: On that day, the Guru had told his grandfather (Bahadur Shah), That he (the Guru) had blessed him (Bahadur Shah) with a sovereignty. The Guru had made his grandfather a sovereign with an active support, Otherwise how could he become sovereign without Guru's (support). (6)
lines: On that day, the Guru had told his grandfather (Bahadur Shah),
That he (the Guru) had blessed him (Bahadur Shah) with a sovereignty.
The Guru had made his grandfather a sovereign with an active support,
Otherwise how could he become sovereign without Guru's (support).

blocks.text: Azam Shah11 was more powerful than his grandfather, As he had the support of a very powerful armed force. How could his grandfather vanquish Azam Khan (without Guru's support), And how could his grandfather harass Azam Khan (Without Guru's support)? (7)
lines: Azam Shah11 was more powerful than his grandfather,
As he had the support of a very powerful armed force.
How could his grandfather vanquish Azam Khan (without Guru's support),
And how could his grandfather harass Azam Khan (Without Guru's support)?

blocks.text: In this way, Farukhsiar refused to oblige the slanderers, Nor did he snap his relations with the House of Nanak. When quite a number of days passed without any incident, The (Guru's) slanderers returned again to incite the emperor. (8)
lines: In this way,
Farukhsiar refused to oblige the slanderers,
Nor did he snap his relations with the House of Nanak.
When quite a number of days passed without any incident,
The (Guru's) slanderers returned again to incite the emperor.
